business_problem: PayPal needed to give employees conversational access to company data at enterprise scale without requiring SQL, dashboards, or intermediary engineering teams, while still meeting strict security and compliance requirements.
solution_summary: PayPal describes a multi-year effort to unify data systems across the company and create a real-time, AI-ready foundation that could support applied AI use cases. On top of that foundation, PayPal deployed an AI-powered internal agent that lets employees ask natural-language questions about data instead of writing SQL or waiting for specialists. The page says the implementation connects systems to enable real-time data access and references governed conversational analytics with Looker and MCP. PayPal's engineering teams built a custom architecture around the experience so credentials remain encrypted and every interaction is audited, allowing the system to satisfy rigorous security and compliance requirements while still serving self-service analytics. In practice, the stack turns a centralized data platform into a governed serving layer for thousands of employees and supports faster internal decisions, with adjacent impact mentioned for false declines, fraud detection, and customer experience improvements.
